results.fact: Total elevation gain (gain_ft vs loss_ft vs itinerary)
results.evidence: Devore Peak's summit is 8,382 ft and the trip starts at Lake Chelan level (Weaver Point, ~1,100-1,160 ft), so the car-to-car gain cannot be under ~7,200 ft; the itinerary (3,100 + 4,200 + 300) and loss_ft both say 7,600. A 2022 trip report camped at the 4,200 ft Devore/Bird Creek junction and logged ~3,500 ft for the camp-to-summit day alone, which is what gain_ft=3500 appears to hold. The same arithmetic makes descent_text's '~4,000+ ft of elevation loss back to Weaver Point' an understatement (summit to lake is ~7,200 ft), so that copy is corrected too.

results.evidence: dist_km=5.6 km (3.5 mi) matches only the camp-to-summit leg (a 2022 party logged ~7 mi round trip from the 4,200 ft camp), so it is not the one-way approach. But the true one-way figure depends on the start: Bird Creek Camp is ~4 mi up the Devore Creek trail from Weaver Point (so ~7.5 mi one-way from Weaver Point), while the waypoints measure 11 mi from the Harlequin Bridge shuttle stop. The itinerary's own day-1 '9 miles' also disagrees with its '4-5 miles' note. No two sources give a one-way distance for the same start, so no patch.

results.fact: Whether fixed rappel anchors exist on the crux/summit step
results.correct_value: Slung (webbing) rappel anchors are in place at the summit-ridge edge and above the crux step; there are no bolts or chains
results.evidence: Gilbertson's trip report found a rap anchor at the edge of the summit ridge, another on top of the crux pitch, and used a good rap anchor at the summit block. A 2022 party describes a conveniently located rap station at the top of the unavoidable 4th-class step and made two rappels; a 2015 report found old, raggedy webbing at the belay station and backed it up. descent_text's 'no fixed hardware ... build a natural anchor' is the outlier; rappels, baseFinding, detailed_rack and pitch_detail already agree.

patches.fact: Whether fixed rappel anchors exist on the crux/summit step
patches.find: there are no fixed bolts, chains, or any other fixed hardware on this route, so if you choose to rappel it rather than downclimb, you'll build a natural anchor (webbing/cord around a horn or block) and retrieve your gear, or downclimb it with a spot/handline.
patches.replace: there are no bolts or chains, but slung webbing rappel anchors have been found in place at the edge of the summit ridge and above the step — inspect and back up any old webbing before trusting it (carry spare cord), or downclimb it with a spot/handline.

results.fact: Seasonal guidance omits the season it's quoted for
results.evidence: A route write-up for the Colchuck Glacier approach gives late May through early July as the easiest window, with late season turning the glacier to bare ice; the Mountaineers route notes also advise against late season. Dated ascents fall in May (2009, 2012) and early July (2021, 2022), and an August 2019 party found hairy blue ice. The stored monthBreakdown (Dec-Apr, 'late winter') describes a winter couloir and contradicts season (May-Jul), the itinerary and climate; it is replaced, and the watch_out line stops quoting it.

results.evidence: No source gives a time for Der Dihedral itself. It finishes on the Backbone Ridge / NE Arete terrain, for which climbers usually allot ~12 hours of climbing, and one party took ~18 hours car to car (about 13-14 hours camp to camp once the lake approach is removed); a Backbone party took ~2 hours from the summit back to camp. Parties on the Triple Couloirs line (whose entry gully this is) report a 30 m rope, 2 x 60 m half ropes, and a thin 60 m rope, and the row's own corrections admit the 30 m was an estimate. Sources support both lengths, so neither the gear list's 60 m nor rope_length_m=30 can be settled; no patch.

Dated ascents of the couloir line fall in winter and spring: early winter (guide-service report), January 6 2013, March 31 2018, April 29 2017 and May 7 2023. best_season, climate, itinerary.cal and seasonal_guidance (Dec-Apr) already describe late winter to spring; season's Apr-Jul was the outlier and also carried an explanation it should not hold.
